title: (fix) O3-6110: Show the patient banner in workspaces on tablet and outside the patient chart
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

On tablet-sized screens, patient-chart data-entry workspaces fill the whole screen and cover the persistent patient banner, so clinicians lose sight of which patient they are documenting on. Many workspaces either omitted a patient header entirely or only rendered one at certain breakpoints, and some lacked the patient UUID needed to display it, so the active patient's name and identifier were invisible precisely when the workspace occupied the full screen. This made it easy to enter data for the wrong patient and left no on-screen confirmation of who was being worked on. This PR renders the compact patient banner at the top of the affected workspaces whenever they run outside the patient chart, and at tablet widths when they run inside the chart, so the banner is not duplicated at desktop widths where the chart banner is still visible. It threads the patient UUID through the wrappers that were missing it, resolves a full FHIR patient for the banner when a caller supplies a partial or REST representation, and shows the primary identifier in the visit-form details tile so the active patient is identifiable on tablet.

title: (fix) O3-6097: Fix inverted labels on the free text dosage toggle
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary The "Free text dosage" toggle in the drug order form was showing the opposite of its actual state. It read "On" while switched off (structured Dose / Route / Frequency fields showing) and "Off" once switched on (free-text box showing). The same thing happened in other languages, e.g. French showed "Activé" while the toggle was off. This could lead a clinician to believe structured dosing was selected while they were actually typing into the free-text box, which is how orders with no dose, route, frequency or duration were ending up saved and stuck in Active Medications. The cause was the labels passed to Carbon's `Toggle` in `drug-order-form.component.tsx`. Carbon shows `labelA` when unchecked and `labelB` when checked, and we had them the other way round. I swapped them so the label now matches the toggle state, and added a test that checks the label text in both states. No translation changes are needed since the `on` / `off` keys already exist. ## Screenshots Free text dosage switched on, label now reads "On": ## Related Issue https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/O3-6097 ## Other N/A

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

This PR addresses [O3-6047](https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/O3-6047) by introducing a shared `WorkspaceBackButton` component in `@openmrs/esm-patient-common-lib` and migrating patient chart workspaces away from duplicated inline Carbon buttons and CSS overrides.

### Context & Implementation
In patient chart workspaces, back buttons duplicated JSX and SCSS styling overrides (`order: 1` to move Carbon's `renderIcon` to the left of the label, and `!important` to override the margin and fill Carbon gives it).

1. **Shared Component**: Created `WorkspaceBackButton` in `packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/workspace-back-button/` that:
   - Takes `label: string` and `onClick: MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>`.
   - Renders `ArrowLeftIcon` directly before the text label as children of a ghost Carbon `Button`, cleanly placing the icon to the left without CSS flex order hacks or `!important` overrides.
   - Renders the arrow at 16px. Carbon's `cds--btn__icon` class used to force button icons to 16px, so the old `size={24}` never applied.
   - Provides consistent spacing via `workspace-back-button.scss` (`@carbon/layout`).
   - Exported from `@openmrs/esm-patient-common-lib`.
2. **Workspaces Migrated**:
   - `packages/esm-patient-medications-app`: migrated `AddDrugOrder` (`add-drug-order.component.tsx`), deleted redundant `.backButton` SCSS rule in `add-drug-order.scss`.
   - `packages/esm-patient-orders-app`: migrated `AddGeneralOrder` (`add-general-order.component.tsx`), deleted redundant `.backButton` SCSS rule in `orderable-concept-search.scss`.
   - `packages/esm-patient-tests-app`: migrated `AddLabOrder` (`add-test-order.component.tsx`), deleted redundant `.backButton` SCSS rule in `add-test-order.scss`.
3. **Tests & Quality**:
   - Added unit test suite `workspace-back-button.test.tsx` verifying label rendering and click interaction using React Testing Library (`getByRole`).
   - Verified that all unit tests pass across all 4 packages (`esm-patient-common-lib`, `esm-patient-medications-app`, `esm-patient-orders-app`, `esm-patient-tests-app`).

title: (fix) O3-6044: Provide WHO z-score reference data to the Angular form engine
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

This PR registers the WHO reference data that the z-score helpers in the Angular form engine expect, so forms that calculate growth z-scores can be saved.

The helpers take the reference data as their first argument, e.g. `calcWeightForHeightZscore(weightForHeightRef, height, weight)`, and AMPATH's POC triage form uses all three. esm-form-entry-app never registered `weightForHeightRef`, `heightForAgeRef` or `bmiForAgeRef`, so these expressions fail and the expression runner sets each z-score field to `false`. The field shows `0`, which looks like a normal z-score. The form still passes validation, but the backend rejects `false` as the value of a numeric obs (`For input string: "false"`), so the encounter can't be saved. AMPATH's ng2-amrs registers these references in `getPatientObject`. O3's version leaves them out.

Now `wireDataSources`:

- Registers each reference the form schema mentions, with the data for the patient's sex and age. Height-for-age uses the under-5 table through day 1,856, where that table ends, and the 5 to 19 year table from month 61, so there's no month without a reference after the fifth birthday. BMI-for-age has no under-5 table, so it has no reference until month 61.
- Registers a reference that doesn't apply to the patient (aged 18 or over, sex other than F or M, or no birth date) as `null`, which the helpers handle. Leaving it out is what makes the field `false`.
- Loads each table with a dynamic `import()`, so forms that don't use the references don't download them, and forms that do load at most two tables.

Seven of the eight tables are copied from esm-form-engine-lib and are identical to ng2-amrs's copies. The girls' 5 to 19 height-for-age table there is a copy of the boys' one, so `hfa_girls_5_above.json` here is generated from WHO's girls' height-for-age z-score tables instead. Each column is M * (1 + k * S), rounded half to even to three decimals, which regenerates the boys' table byte for byte from WHO's boys' tables. `resolveJsonModule` is on so TypeScript can check the JSON imports.

In a production build, the tables are eight lazy chunks of 28 to 259 KiB (7 to 58 KiB gzipped). The app's existing chunks grow by 2.1 KiB in total, for the loader and the chunk map.

On tests:

- `form-creation.service.spec.ts` builds the z-score questions from AMPATH's triage form with the real `FormFactory`. Without this change, both calculation tests get `false`. With it, a 3-year-old girl gets the expected weight-for-height and height-for-age z-scores, and an 8-year-old boy gets the expected height-for-age and BMI-for-age ones. A 15-year-old girl at 160 cm gets `-1` against the girls' reference, where the boys' table gave `-2`. A form that doesn't mention the references doesn't get them registered.
- `zscore-references.spec.ts` covers the row chosen by age in days or months, including the month after the fifth birthday, returning only the references a form uses, and the cases where no reference data applies. It also checks that each girls' table differs from the boys' one, and spot-checks the 5 to 19 height-for-age medians against WHO's tables.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Visit attributes with the `Date` data type were broken in the visit form and could show the wrong day in the patient banner.
- If a date was selected, a user couldn't submit the form. The button didn't appear disabled, there was no error message, but clicking the button just didn't do anything at all. But if you use the React dev tools, you'd see an error logged in the form state.
- The field was never marked invalid because the input was given only `aria-invalid` and not `invalid` and the `invalidText` only renders if `invalid` is set.
- The field now parses the fixed date into a `YYYY-MM-DD` string, because that is what the backend would expect.
- When editing a visit, the REST API returns the saved date as midnight in the server's offset (e.g. `2026-10-15T00:00:00.000+0530`). The field now uses only the date part, so the picker does not shift the day when the browser and server offsets are different.
- The tag in the patient banner used `new Date(value)`, so a browser behind the server showed the previous day (e.g. 19 Oct for a date saved as 20 Oct, with a UTC server and a browser in America/New_York). It now formats the date part as local midnight.

## Summary

This follows up on #3712, which lazy-loads the vitals and biometrics charts. It makes the first switch to the chart view smoother:

The skeleton keeps the card at its final height, and keeps `role="progressbar"` and a "Loading" label for screen readers.

The rendered chart view is 482px tall: the 400px chart plus its label and the tab panel's padding. So the skeleton is 466px with 8px margins. Both cards measure 532px with the skeleton and with the chart.

title: (fix) Allow a death date on the day of birth ahead of UTC
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary
Fixes the mark patient deceased form rejecting a death on the patient's day of birth in timezones ahead of UTC.

The form parsed the FHIR `birthDate`, a date-only string like `1972-04-04`, with `new Date()`, which reads it as UTC midnight. In Nairobi that's 03:00 on the day of birth, but the date picker returns local midnight, so a death on the same day failed "Death date cannot be before the date of birth". It now uses `parseDate` from the framework, which reads the date as local midnight. This also stops the date picker offering the day before birth in timezones behind UTC.

That alone wasn't enough on a UTC server. `markPatientDeceased` sent `deathDate` as a full timestamp, and the backend rejects a death date earlier than the stored birthdate, which is midnight in the server's timezone. From Nairobi, the day of birth went out as 21:00 UTC the day before and failed with "Death date must be after birth date". `deathDate` is now sent as `YYYY-MM-DD`, which the server reads in its own timezone, the same way it stores birthdates.

Today is the exception and is sent as the current time. A plain date for today is still in the future on a server behind the browser's timezone (00:00 to 03:00 in Nairobi against a UTC server) and would be rejected as a future date. That probably still leaves a patient born and dying today within that window, since the stored birthdate would then be in the future on the server.

The new form test switches to `Africa/Nairobi` and submits a death date on the day of birth. The new `markPatientDeceased` tests check that a past date is sent as `YYYY-MM-DD` and today as the current time.

## Screenshots

## Summary
This PR makes `invalidateVisitByUuid` actually revalidate the visit it's given. It was passing a `RegExp` to SWR's `mutate`, but SWR only treats a function as a key filter. The regex got serialized as a single literal key that didn't match anything in the cache, so the call did nothing. I've swapped it for a key filter function, like the other helpers in `revalidation-utils.ts`, and added a test.

Starting or editing a visit, switching the visit context, and restoring a deleted visit all store this helper as the patient chart's `mutateVisitContext`. So after any of those, later `mutateVisitContext` calls (order basket, form entry, deleting an encounter, the vitals launcher) didn't refetch the visit until you reloaded the page. The medications table also calls it directly, and I've fixed the orders table, which was calling it eagerly instead of passing a function.

This stops the patient chart from loading code for things the summary page doesn't show:

- `esm-patient-chart-app` no longer lists `lodash-es` in `peerDependencies`. That made it a shared module, and since the app shell doesn't provide it, the chart app loaded the whole package (77 KiB) for three functions.

I built these four modules from `main` and from this branch, swapped each set into a build of today's `next`, and ran the same workflows as the 3.8.0 benchmark: the chart summary, visits, clinical forms, the order basket with a drug search, and patient search.

## Summary

When saving changes to an existing general order fails, the general order form now shows the backend's error message as the snackbar subtitle, falling back to the error's own message. Previously it passed the raw error object from `postOrder` as the `subtitle`.

This uses the same `responseBody?.error?.message ?? message` lookup as the order basket tile and the lab results form in this package.

title: (fix) O3-6004: Make lab result entry safe to retry
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Lab result entry now saves the results and discontinues the test order in a single encounter request, then marks the order as fulfilled. The backend saves inline orders inside the same transaction as the obs, so if the discontinue fails, the results aren't saved either.

Previously `updateOrderResult` made three separate requests: post the obs to the encounter, discontinue the order, then set `fulfillerStatus` to `COMPLETED`. If the second or third request failed, the results were already saved but the order wasn't `COMPLETED`, so the form stayed in create mode. Clicking Save again posted the obs a second time, leaving duplicate results on the order. If the fulfiller update was the one that failed, it got worse: every retry added another copy of the results and then failed on the discontinue, because the backend returns a 500 when you stop an order that's already stopped. The order could never be completed from the form.

When an order already has saved results but isn't `COMPLETED`, the form now fills in the saved values, and saving updates those obs instead of creating new ones. It then discontinues the order only if its `dateStopped` is still empty, and marks it as fulfilled. This also covers results left behind by the old code. Before saving, the form fetches the order's encounter to check for saved results, rather than trusting the results it loaded earlier, so a retry clicked before the form has refreshed still takes the right path. If that check fails, nothing is saved. Saved values only fill in fields the user hasn't changed, so a refetch that lands after an edit doesn't overwrite it.

Sending the discontinue inside the encounter request follows the same pattern as `postOrdersOnNewEncounter` in the order basket. The fulfiller update stays a separate call, as in the laboratory app, because the encounter request can't set it. Repeating the fulfiller update is harmless.

## Screenshots

### Before
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0565e14-0490-4405-bd61-e9ce2dbd0c9a

### After
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3155958-ac22-48a8-a4e3-3826ba116e2a


## Related Issue

https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-6004

## Other

I reproduced the duplicate against a local backend (core 2.8.10-SNAPSHOT, webservices.rest 3.5.0) by injecting a 500 on `POST /order`. After one retry, the order had two identical results. With this change, I ran four scenarios through the UI and checked each one over REST:

- The fulfiller update fails, then Save again.
- The encounter request commits but the browser gets a 500.
- Results left over from the old code, with the order still active.
- The fulfiller update fails, then Save again straight away while the form's own refetch of the saved results is held back.

Each one ended with one result, one discontinue order, and the order `COMPLETED`.

Unit tests cover the single encounter request, skipping the fulfiller update when saving the results fails, discontinuing only an active order, fetching only the order's own results, updating saved results instead of posting them again (including on a retry before the form refreshes), saving nothing when the check for saved results fails, and keeping the user's edits when saved results load late. One of the new tests also passes on `main`: skipping the fulfiller update, since the old code also stopped when saving the results failed.

title: (fix) O3-5998: Continue to the requested workspace after starting or selecting a visit
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary
When a chart action needs a visit and the patient has none, `useStartVisitIfNeeded` shows a visit prompt and waits for the user to start or pick a visit. Neither path continued to the workspace the user asked for, so they had to click the action again. This PR makes both paths continue.

- With RDE off, the start visit dialog passes `onVisitStarted` into the `start-visit-workspace-form` workspace, but the chart's wrapper never read it, so the promise never resolved. The wrapper now accepts `onVisitStarted` and calls it after it sets the visit context.
- With RDE on, selecting a visit resolved the promise straight away. Setting a new visit context makes the patient chart relaunch its workspace group once the visit is refetched, and `launchWorkspaceGroup2` closes every open window when the group props change. So the resumed workspace was closed before it rendered. The RDE-off path hits the same thing once the callback is wired up.

To fix the second part, the patient chart store records which visit the workspace group was last launched with, and the chart sets it after each successful relaunch. `useStartVisitIfNeeded` resolves true only once that matches the new visit context. Under RDE, closing the switcher after a selection no longer resolves false first.

The new store field is optional and its setter is a plain exported function, so the existing `usePatientChartStore` mocks in the other apps don't need to change.

## Screenshots

### Before

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59c47c95-f90f-4020-b47f-8b55c0afab76

### After

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0850d61e-c25a-42f6-9e64-e7cbfad1ed17

## Related Issue
https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/O3-5998

## Other
This touches the same block in `useStartVisitIfNeeded` as #3619, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. Renew in #3619 continues after the prompt once both are in.

With RDE off, cancelling the prompt or discarding the visit form still leaves the promise pending. The ticket explains why that's out of scope.

body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary The Add attachment dialog took an `allowedExtensions` prop but never read it: every step fetched the backend's `attachments.allowedFileExtensions` itself, so the visit note form's request to leave out PDFs did nothing. The helper text advertised pdf, a PDF went through to the review step, and the note ended up with a blank thumbnail. The dialog also told the user "Upload complete" the moment the caller's `saveFile` resolved, which in the note form only stages the file for upload on save. The dialog now puts the caller's list on its context and falls back to the backend list only when the caller passes nothing. The upload and review steps read from the context instead of fetching on their own. The success snackbar can be switched off with `showUploadSnackbar`; the note form does that, and passes `undefined` instead of an empty list while the backend list is loading, since an empty list means nothing is allowed. Building the error message no longer pops the last extension off the shared list, which mutated it for the next attempt. The staged thumbnail's alt now falls back to the file name when there's no description, and the visit-note e2e spec checks that thumbnail instead of the removed toast. Verified against a local backend: the note form's dialog lists only jpeg, jpg and png, refuses a PDF before the review step, and staging a PNG shows no toast. The Attachments page still passes the backend list and behaves as before. ## Screenshots PDF refused in the note form's dialog: PNG staged with no "Upload complete" toast: ## Related Issue https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5987 ## Other Found while working on O3-5986 (#3668). - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

An image uploaded through a visit note saves and shows up on the Attachments page, but it's missing when we reopen the note to edit it. The form only ever sent the patient when uploading, so the obs ended up encounterless, and the edit form never looked for saved images anyway.

Images added to a note now go up with the note's encounter UUID, so the attachment obs lands on that encounter. When we edit the note, the form loads the attachments recorded on that encounter and shows them ahead of any new uploads. Only images added in this session live in the form state, so editing just the text uploads nothing and adding another image uploads only that one. The create form makes no attachments request since there's no encounter to look up yet.

Saved images are read only in the form. We don't offer a remove control for them on purpose: `DELETE /attachment/{uuid}` purges the obs and then voids the encounter when no obs are left ([AttachmentResource.voidEncounterIfEmpty](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-attachments/blob/master/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/attachments/rest/AttachmentResource.java)), which would take a note with blank text and its diagnoses down with it. Removing a saved image needs to void the obs instead; that's O3-5990.

Older notes whose images were saved without an encounter keep showing on the Attachments page. We don't guess them onto a note.

Because the images now sit on the note's encounter, they also show up in the encounter expansion on the Visits page, where a complex obs used to render as `ATT IMAGE ATTACHMENT: m3ks` (the REST display string is the attachments module's storage marker). The observations list now shows a complex obs as its caption, or the file name parsed from `valueComplex`, as a link. Clicking it opens a new read-only `attachment-preview-modal` from the attachments app (file name, caption, image or PDF); the href still points at the bytes endpoint so the file can be opened in a new tab. The Attachments page keeps its full-screen preview with the delete action, and the image/PDF rendering the two share now lives in one `AttachmentMedia` component. The visit and encounter representations fetch `valueComplex` and `comment` for that. The attachment bytes URL was hand-built in three apps; it's now `getAttachmentBytesUrl` in esm-patient-common-lib.

Depends on openmrs/openmrs-esm-core#1887 for the new `createAttachment` and `useAttachments` parameters. That has merged and main already resolves `@openmrs/esm-framework` to the `next` build that carries it (10.0.1-pre.5452), so this PR needs no lockfile change.

Verified end to end against a local backend with that framework build: the obs sits on the note encounter, the saved image shows on reopen, a text-only edit doesn't re-upload, a second image adds without duplicating, and the Attachments page still lists everything. Exercised JPEG and PNG through the picker, a webcam capture, and a PDF on the same encounter (hidden from the note's Image section, still on the Attachments page).

title: (fix) O3-5976: Fix Angular locale import requesting non-existent .mjs files
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The form engine lazily loads Angular locale data for the user's language, but the dynamic import only matched `.mjs` files. `@angular/common/locales` only ships `.js` files, so the import never found a file and `registerLocaleData()` never ran for any locale.

`LOCALE_ID` is still set to the user's language, so Angular's `date` pipe throws for any locale other than English. For example, with the language set to French, a form with a question that shows a previous value (via `historicalExpression`) fails to render.

This PR:

- Imports the locale files from `../../../node_modules/@angular/common/locales/${locale}.js`. Importing through the package name doesn't work here: `@angular/common` only exports `./locales/*`, and webpack needs to resolve the `locales` directory itself to build the lazy import.
- Limits the bundled files with `webpackInclude: /locales[\/\\][a-z]{2}\.js$/`. This emits one chunk for each of the 133 two-letter base locales and leaves out the `extra/` and `global/` variants. The pattern accepts both `/` and `\` because webpack matches it against the absolute file path, which uses backslashes on Windows.
- Logs a warning when the locale data can't be loaded (for example, an unsupported locale or a failed chunk request) instead of leaving an unhandled rejection.

## Screenshots

title: (fix) O3-5957: Correct MUAC color code age boundaries
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below.
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

`getMuacColorCode` (in `vitals-biometrics-form.utils.ts`) had inconsistent age-bracket boundary conditions. Patients aged exactly 10 or 18 got no color code set at all, for any MUAC value, because adjacent brackets both excluded the boundary age.

**Update after review:** the initial fix only closed the gap without checking which side of each boundary was correct. Per [@denniskigen's review](#), age brackets and MUAC cut-offs now follow the Uganda Ministry of Health IMAM Guidelines (Jan 2016), Table 2: Summary of Classification of Acute Malnutrition (https://platform.who.int/docs/default-source/mca-documents/policy-documents/guideline/UGA-CH-38-03-GUIDELINE-2016-eng-IMAM-Guidelines-for-Uganda-Jan-2016.pdf).

Since `age` is the whole number of years extracted from the patient's birth date, each bracket's **lower bound is inclusive** (e.g. a patient turning exactly 5 falls into the "5 to <10 years" bracket, not "6-59 months"). The brackets are now:

| Age | SAM (red) | MAM (yellow) | Healthy (green) |
|---|---|---|---|
| under 5y | <11.5cm | 11.5–<12.5cm | ≥12.5cm |
| 5 to <10y | <13.5cm | 13.5–<14.5cm | ≥14.5cm |
| 10 to <15y | <16.0cm | 16.0–<18.5cm | ≥18.5cm |
| 15 to <18y | <18.5cm | 18.5–<21.0cm | ≥21.0cm |
| 18y+ (adults) | <19.0cm | 19.0–<22.0cm | ≥22.0cm |

This also splits the old combined "10 to <18" bracket into the two separate brackets (10-<15 and 15-<18) that the guideline actually specifies, and corrects their MUAC thresholds (previously both used 16.5/19.0, which matched neither bracket).

Verified against the reviewer's own example: a 5-year-old with MUAC 13.0cm now correctly classifies as red/SAM (previously green under the first pass, and previously no color at all before any fix).

Before any fix, 3/3 boundary-age tests fail:
getMuacColorCode (3)
× sets a color code for a healthy 5-year-old (age boundary)
× sets a color code for a 10-year-old (age boundary)
× sets a color code for an 18-year-old (age boundary)

After the guideline-aligned fix, all tests pass, including a new test for the 15-year-old boundary and the reviewer's 5y/13.0cm example:
getMuacColorCode (4)
✓ classifies a 5-year-old with MUAC 13.0cm as SAM (red), per the 5-<10y bracket
✓ sets a color code for a 10-year-old (age boundary)
✓ sets a color code for a 15-year-old (age boundary)
✓ sets a color code for an 18-year-old (age boundary), classified with adults

Full esm-patient-vitals-app test suite also passes.

## Screenshots

N/A  this is a pure logic fix in a utility function, not directly rendered UI. The `useMuacColors` config flag is off by default, so behavior is covered by unit tests rather than a visual screenshot.

## Related Issue

https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/O3-5957

## Other

Found via direct code review of the vitals/biometrics module. Boundary-age direction and bracket split corrected per review feedback, using the Uganda MoH IMAM Guidelines as the source of truth.

title: (feat) O3-5823: Capture diagnosis rank and certainty in the visit note
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The visit note form previously hardcoded `certainty: 'PROVISIONAL'` on every diagnosis it saved, and encoded rank in which of two search boxes (primary/secondary) the clinician typed into. Neither rank nor certainty was ever an explicit clinical choice, and neither was visible anywhere after saving.

This PR makes both values deliberate on entry. Certainty also shows in the visits table through the styleguide's `DiagnosisTags` (openmrs/openmrs-esm-core#1881). The design follows the discussion on [Talk](https://talk.openmrs.org/t/50125):

- **One diagnosis search box** replaces the primary/secondary pair. Each added diagnosis renders as a single row — **Primary checkbox → name → ⋯ actions → remove** — under a "Primary" column header. New diagnoses appear at the top. When a note is opened for editing, stored primaries are sorted first once; after that rows stay where they are, so toggling Primary never moves a row out from under the pointer.
- **Confirmed by default; no auto-primary.** Certainty is changed through the row's ⋯ menu ("Mark as provisional" / "Mark as confirmed"), and a provisional diagnosis shows a leading "?". Primary is never pre-ticked, so the clinical choice stays explicit. The helper text states the default: "Diagnoses are recorded as confirmed unless marked provisional."
- **The certainty action is offered only for diagnosis-class concepts.** Concepts picked from the search already qualify (the search is filtered to the configured `diagnosisConceptClass`). When a note is opened for editing, the classes of its coded diagnoses are fetched in a single `conceptreferences` request (`useDiagnosisConceptClasses`, cached), so Symptom/Finding-class concepts recorded by other forms keep their stored certainty and "?" but get no ⋯. Free-text diagnoses keep the action. While the lookup is pending the action is withheld; if it fails — or the endpoint omits a reference — the action is kept rather than stranding a stored provisional diagnosis.
- **Primary-required validation** (`isPrimaryDiagnosisRequired`, default on) is validated at the group level and rendered once beneath the diagnosis list: a live warning (Carbon's `WarningAltFilled`) as soon as diagnoses exist without a primary, turning into an error (`WarningFilled`, red, `role="alert"`) once a save has been blocked by it. It clears the moment Primary is ticked, and a blocked save focuses the topmost Primary checkbox (or the search input when nothing is selected). Every Primary checkbox is described by that message via `aria-describedby`, and on tablets the checkbox has a 32px touch target matching the actions beside it.
- **Editing pre-selects stored values.** Rank or certainty values outside the known enums (possible from other REST writers) fall back to secondary/confirmed rather than being silently rewritten; a missing certainty is displayed as confirmed (`mapEncounter` defaults it), matching the form's presumption rather than the old `'PROVISIONAL'` fallback. Previously, diagnoses with rank outside {1,2} were silently *deleted* on edit. Non-coded diagnoses now survive the edit round-trip, and rows are keyed by a client-side draft id so duplicate concepts or non-coded entries no longer collide.
- **Visit-level data**: the visits-widget representation now fetches `certainty`, and `dedupeDiagnoses` merges duplicates across a visit's encounters with documented, order-independent rules — rank = mi

title: (fix) O3-5953: Use the active or selected visit when renewing medication orders
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary
Renew opened the order basket with the original order's visit as the workspace's visit context. When that visit was closed, the renewal encounter was created inside it and dated into its window, so a renewal made today was filed under a visit from months ago. Dispensing filters Active prescriptions by encounter date, so those renewals didn't show up there once the original visit was older than the expiry window.

Renew now goes through `useStartVisitIfNeeded`, like Add, and opens the basket without the medication's group props, so the basket uses the chart's active or selected visit. The renewal is only added once a visit is available, and it's appended to whatever the basket holds by then. Cancelling the prompt leaves the basket as it was.

To support that, the start visit dialog now reports cancellation. Its Cancel and close buttons call a new `onCancel` prop, which `useStartVisitIfNeeded` resolves as false.

Modify and Discontinue are unchanged, and still use the order's own encounter and visit.

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

On the pinned @carbon/react 1.x, the classic OverflowMenu pulls `aria-label` out of its props and applies it to the menu body (the `<ul role="menu">`), not to the trigger button. The trigger's accessible name comes from `iconDescription`, which defaults to "Options". We were passing labels like "Encounter table actions menu" and "Edit or delete allergy" via `aria-label`, so they never reached the trigger and screen readers announced a generic "Options" for every overflow menu in the app.

This passes the label through `iconDescription` instead, in the visit timeline, encounters table, orders and medications tables, and the allergies, conditions, procedures, programs, and vitals action menus. The conditions menu label was a hardcoded English string, so it's now translated. Unit tests and e2e specs that located the triggers by the "Options" name now use the real labels.

## Screenshots

The only visual change is the trigger's hover tooltip, which now shows the descriptive label instead of "Options".

## Related Issue

## Other

Heads up for e2e: openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-management#2711 adds a spec (`e2e/specs/queue-entry-visit-summary.spec.ts`) that locates this trigger with `getByRole('button', { name: /options/i })`. Once this lands, the encounter actions trigger is named "Encounter table actions menu", so that spec needs a coordinated update.

title: (fix) Clean build outputs before bundle size comparison
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a conventional commit label.
- [ ] My work is based on designs. Not applicable because this is a CI-only change.
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The compressed-size action builds the PR and base revisions sequentially in the same workspace. When the base build is restored from the Turborepo cache, Rspack does not run and stale PR chunks remain in each package `dist` directory. This causes renamed chunks to be counted as removed instead of replaced and substantially inflates the reported bundle-size reduction.

This change uses the action-supported `clean-script` hook to run `clean:dist` between measurements. Each of the 22 buildable packages owns a `clean` script scoped to its ignored `dist` directory, while the root script orchestrates those package tasks through Turborepo. The Turborepo `clean` task has caching disabled so cleanup always executes.

The bundle-size workflow validated that all 22 cleanup tasks ran successfully and now reports a 0 B size change for this CI-only PR.

title: (fix) Correct data handling defects in the generic obs widgets
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

This fixes five data handling defects in the generic obs widgets. Each fix has a regression test that fails against the previous code.

1. **The editable horizontal table silently discarded a typed value of 0.** The save guard used `!editingValue`, and Carbon's NumberInput delivers a typed "0" as the number `0`, so entering a legitimate zero (scores, counts) was a no-op with no feedback. The guard now only bails on genuinely empty input.

2. **One observation without an encounter crashed the whole widget.** `Observation.encounter` is optional in FHIR (obs created via REST integrations often have none), but `useObs` dereferenced `resource.encounter.reference` unguarded. Reproduced against a live backend: an obs created without an encounter comes back from this widget's exact FHIR query with no `encounter` field. Encounter-less obs now map cleanly and render as their own rows in the obs table. In the horizontal table, whose columns are keyed by encounter, they simply don't appear. The mapping also previously wrote the encounter display name into the FHIR resource held in the SWR cache (the spread copy shares the nested `encounter` object); it now builds a new object instead.

3. **A configured `decimalPlaces: 0` was ignored.** Both tables tested `decimalPlaces > 0`, so an explicit 0 (which the schema's `inRange(0, 10)` validator allows) fell through to `toFixed(2)` for fractional values. An explicit 0 now rounds to whole numbers.

4. **Numeric columns sorted incorrectly.** Integer values are stored as numbers but fractional values as `toFixed` strings, and the comparator compared them as strings, so "9.50" sorted above "12.50" descending. Numeric columns now compare numeric values.

5. **Sorting the encounter type column crashed when a row had no encounter.** The comparator called `localeCompare` directly on the encounter name, which is undefined for the encounter-less rows introduced by fix 2. It now coalesces to an empty string.

## Screenshots

## Related Issue

## Other

This also renames `_validator` to `_validators` in both config schemas. The config system only reads the plural key, so the `inRange(0, 10)` check on `decimalPlaces` never actually ran.

Two lesser issues spotted in the same review are not addressed here: `useConcepts` calls `showSnackbar` during render, and the graph's configured line colors are keyed by the raw label while the series is named with the translated label, so they miss each other in translated locales.

title: (feat) O3-5889: Support fullWidth configuration for the obs-by-encounter widget
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The obs-by-encounter widget is registered with `"fullWidth": false` in its routes.json meta, and there was no way for implementers to override that. This PR adds a `fullWidth` property (default `false`) to the widget's config schema, so each configured instance can opt into spanning the full width of the dashboard:

```json
"patient-chart-summary-dashboard-slot": {
  "add": ["obs-by-encounter-widget#partograph"],
  "configure": {
    "obs-by-encounter-widget#partograph": { "fullWidth": true }
  }
}
```

To make that work, `DashboardView` now resolves each widget's width from its extension config first, falling back to the extension's routes.json meta.

This also fixes a latent bug. `DashboardView` looked up meta by extension instance id, but `useExtensionSlotMeta` keys its map by extension name. For instances added via config with a `#` suffix, such as `obs-by-encounter-widget#partograph`, the lookup always missed and the widget rendered half width regardless of its registered meta. Reading meta straight off the `AssignedExtension` fixes that, so `#` suffixed instances of other widgets now honor their registered `fullWidth` value too.

## Screenshots

## Related Issue

https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5889

## Other

I deliberately didn't add `fullWidth` to the horizontal obs table's config schema. That schema serves both `obs-table-horizontal-widget-small` (meta `false`) and `obs-table-horizontal-widget` (meta `true`), and a schema default would override the meta for both registrations, flipping the full width one to half width.

title: (test) Route Laboratory worklist tab references through a typed locator
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. <!-- N/A: test-only refactor, no UI -->
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Small follow-up to #3582.

In `e2e/specs/lab-app-results.spec.ts` the Laboratory worklist tab names were written in two forms: as `LaboratoryTab` literals for the panel lookups, and as free-form regexes for the clicks and the page-loaded gate (`/tests ordered/i`, `/in progress/i`, `/completed/i`). The comment above the type says the union is there so a mistyped tab name is a compile error rather than a locator that silently never resolves, but every tab *locator* sat outside it, so an upstream rename needed two edits per tab and the type caught only one of them.

`getByRole`'s `name` option matches the accessible name as a substring, so a literal locates a tab just as well as the regex did. This adds one `worklistTab(tabName: LaboratoryTab)` locator and routes all four tab references through it: the helper's click, and the visibility gate in the first step. The two standalone click lines go away.

Nothing about what the spec asserts changes.

## Screenshots

N/A, test-only change.

## Related Issue

None of its own. Follow-up from reviewing #3582 (O3-5888).

## Other

What I verified rather than assumed:

- `getByRole`'s substring semantics come from Playwright's own type definitions: "By default, matching is case-insensitive and searches for a substring."
- None of the five titles the Laboratory app registers for `lab-panels-slot` (Tests ordered, In progress, Pending review tests, Completed, Declined tests) is a substring of another, checked pairwise against its `routes.json`, so each of the three literals this spec uses resolves to exactly one tab. That holds with `enableReviewingLabResultsBeforeApproval` on as well, which is what adds the fourth tab.
- `searchAndExpandInTab('Tests ordered')` now clicks a tab that is already selected. The Laboratory app renders a controlled `<Tabs selectedIndex={...} onChange={...}>`, and Carbon's `Tab` `onClick` only calls `setSelectedIndex(index)`, which through `useControllableState` resolves to `setSelectedTab(0)` with the index unchanged: no panel switch, no remount, no state churn.

One caveat worth stating plainly: nothing in this repo lints or type-checks `e2e/`. Every turbo `lint`/`typescript` task scopes its inputs to a package's `src/**`, the root workspace has no such script, and both git hooks reduce to those same tasks. So the union is enforced by an editor, not by CI, and the Playwright run is the only automation that touches this file. That is why the E2E job here is the real check, and I could not run it locally.

title: (chore) Typecheck and lint the E2E suite in CI
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The e2e directory is currently excluded from every static check in CI. `yarn verify` runs `turbo run lint typescript test`, which only covers workspaces under `packages/`, and the E2E workflow transpiles the specs without typechecking. So a type error in a spec, fixture, command, or page object never fails a build.

This PR adds an `e2e/tsconfig.json` that extends the root config and covers everything under `e2e/` plus `playwright.config.ts`, and registers two root-level turbo tasks (`//#typescript` and `//#lint`) so `tsc -p e2e` and `eslint e2e` run as part of the existing verify pipeline on every PR. No workflow changes are needed since `turbo run lint typescript test` picks up the root tasks automatically.

The e2e program follows `@openmrs/esm-patient-common-lib` into its source through the package's `src/index.ts` main entry, so `e2e/declarations.d.ts` mirrors the per-package `*.scss` module declaration to keep those imports resolvable.

A few notes on validation:

- The new program covers all 53 TS files under `e2e/` plus `playwright.config.ts` (verified with `tsc --listFilesOnly`), and an injected type error in a spec fails the build.
- The e2e code is already clean, so both checks pass as-is. Same for `eslint e2e`, which the `e2e/**` override in `eslint.config.mjs` was already set up for but nothing ran in CI.
- `yarn verify` passes locally with the two root tasks in the graph.

If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary The visit form's stop-before-start rule always attached its error to `visitStopDate`. When only the times were inverted on a single day, the date picker was flagged red while the offending time picker looked valid. The error now lands on the end time field when the start and stop fall on the same day, and on the end date field when the dates themselves are out of order. Visits whose stop datetime equals their start datetime stay valid: core rejects only a stop before the start, the EMR API closes visits with no non-voided encounters by setting the stop equal to the start, and the form's hh:mm fields drop seconds, so a short real visit collapses onto a single minute when loaded for editing. Tests cover the field routing and the equal-endpoints cases. ## Screenshots ## Related Issue ## Other

## Summary
<!-- Please describe what problems your PR addresses. -->
Follow-up to #3509. `EncountersTable` launches the chart's edit workspaces, which belong to the `patient-chart` group — scoped to chart URLs, with group props only the chart populates. Hosted elsewhere (Service Queues, via the `visit-summary` extension), the window opens with null group props and every action button in the group throws at once, one per registered icon.

Null-safe buttons wouldn't help, as the group is out of scope there regardless; nor would overriding the workspace names, since the exported notes form takes the patient context as workspace props while exported form entry takes it as window
props. Hosts have to do the launching, hence the optional callback. Absent it, chart behaviour is unchanged.

The `.expandedRow > div` rule removed here was already dead — a `<tr>` has no `<div>` child. Repairing it instead would apply `$ui-02` and leave the expanded rows a white block inside their grey gutters.

The remaining changes address findings from the plugin versions supplied by the shared config. body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary A task with a Date-type due date could shift one day earlier whenever it was opened for editing and saved. Repeating the cycle could move the date back again each time. This affected dates whose local calendar date differed from their UTC date, including local-midnight selections in time zones ahead of UTC. The edit form converted the stored date to `YYYY-MM-DD` using `.toISOString().split('T')[0]`. This selected the UTC calendar date and discarded the original time and offset. On save, `parseDate` interpreted that date-only value at local midnight, persisted the shifted instant, and allowed the drift to repeat on the next edit. The form now retains the full ISO instant using `.toISOString()`, matching the value produced by the date picker. Saving an unchanged task therefore preserves the exact stored instant and displays the correct local calendar date. Tests cover: - Displaying the correct local date for an instant near a UTC day boundary in `Africa/Nairobi`. - Preserving the exact due-date instant when an existing task is saved without changing its due date. ## Screenshots **Before:** The edit form shows the shifted due date, `19/08/2026`. **After:** The edit form shows the correct due date, `20/08/2026`. ## Related Issue [O3-5845: Task due date shifts one day earlier every time an existing task is edited and saved](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5845) ## Other This fix prevents further drift but does not repair due dates on tasks that already went through one or more affected edit-save cycles.

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Bumps the `@angular/*` framework train from 20.3.26 to 20.3.27 to close three high-severity Dependabot alerts: GHSA-jj27-h5hq-8x99 (`@angular/core`, `@angular/compiler`) and GHSA-jhpw-976m-542j (`@angular/common`).

Dependabot opened one PR per vulnerable package (#3535, #3536, #3537). Angular framework packages peer-depend on each other at an exact patch version, so bumping a subset leaves peer ranges Yarn reports as non-overlapping. #3535 and #3537 each add two such warnings, while #3536 adds one. Merging all three still leaves eight framework packages at 20.3.26 and three warnings. This moves all eleven together instead, the same way #3501 did for 20.3.26.

`@angular/cdk` and `@angular/material` stay at 20.2.14, since they track the Components train and peer on `^20.0.0 || ^21.0.0`. `@angular/cli`, `@angular-devkit/*` and `@schematics/angular` stay put too, since they're on their own version line and already float to 20.3.32.

Validated locally, against `main` as the baseline:

- `yarn install` reports one peer warning, the pre-existing `@ng-select/ng-select` one. Same as main.
- `yarn workspace @openmrs/esm-form-entry-app build` succeeds.
- `yarn dedupe --check` reports the same 5 dedupable packages as main, so this adds no dedupe debt.
- `@openmrs/ngx-formentry` and `@openmrs/ngx-file-uploader` peer on `^20.0.0` and `^20.0.2` respectively, so both are satisfied. ngx-formentry ships partial declarations that the 20.3.27 `compiler-cli` links at build time without complaint.

Neither vulnerable feature is actually used here, so this closes the alerts rather than fixing a live exposure. The app has no Angular built-in i18n (it uses ngx-translate, and there are no `i18n` attributes in its templates or in the ngx-formentry dist), and no SSR, so there's no `HttpTransferCache`.

Supersedes #3535, #3536 and #3537. Those should be closed rather than merged.

title: (feat) O3-5850: Support concept reference ranges in the Angular form engine
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Concept reference ranges (Platform 2.7+) never reached forms rendered by the Angular form engine (AFE). The vitals widget and the results viewer both use them already, but a numeric question in an AFE form was still bounded only by whatever `questionOptions.min` / `questionOptions.max` the schema author happened to hardcode. So a form would accept a value that the backend then rejects, and none of the age/sex/pregnancy based ranges applied.

The cause is straightforward: nothing in `esm-form-entry-app` ever fetched `/conceptreferencerange`. `QuestionFactory.addValidators` in ngx-formentry builds the min/max validators purely from the schema, and we hand it the schema untouched.

### What changed

- `ConceptReferenceRangeResourceService` fetches the ranges for the concepts of every numeric question in the schema, for the patient the form is being filled for.
- `FeWrapperComponent` loads them alongside the previous encounter, once the schema is known.
- `FormCreationService` narrows each numeric question to the absolute bounds of the range that applies, right before the form is built.

A few decisions worth calling out:

- Only `lowAbsolute` / `hiAbsolute` are used. That mirrors what the backend validates against, and matches the [docs](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/docs/pages/178782250) ("only absolute values are used"). Normal and critical bounds are for flagging, which the Angular engine has no UI for.
- A bound already in the schema is never widened. If the schema says `max: 50` and the range says 43, you get 43; if the schema says 30 and the range says 25, you get 30. Whichever is stricter wins, same idea as core applying the strictest of several matching ranges.
- Questions can name their concept either by UUID or by a reference like `CIEL:5089`, so those get resolved through the schema's `conceptReferences` map before matching.
- Bounds are written back as strings, which is how the [form schema](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-json-schemas/blob/main/form.schema.json) declares `min` and `max`. Matters more than it looks: a `lowAbsolute` of 0 written as a number would be falsy and the engine would then skip both validators.

Nothing changes on servers that don't have the resource. A failed request, an older backend, or offline mode all fall back to an empty map and the form loads exactly as it does today.

### For form authors and implementers

No schema changes are required. Numeric `obs` questions using `number` or `decimal` automatically use patient-specific absolute reference ranges when their concept resolves by UUID or mapping. Existing `min` and `max` values still apply when they are stricter.

This only applies to implementations using `@openmrs/esm-form-entry-app`, the Angular Form Engine integration. The default O3 React Form Engine does not use this code. The backend must also have concept reference ranges configured, and both effective bounds must be available.

### Known limitation

The engine only wires up the min and max validators when both are present (`if (questionOptions.max && questionOptions.min)` in `QuestionFactory.addValidators`). A concept with only one absolute bound therefore still gets no validation. Left alone here since fixing it means a change in ngx-formentry, happy to file that separately.

title: (fix) O3-5841: Sort Vitals and Biometrics tables in the direction the header arrow indicates
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The Vitals and Biometrics tables sorted in the opposite direction to the one indicated by the column header arrow: an ascending (↑) arrow put the newest reading at the top, and a descending (↓) arrow put the oldest reading at the top.

Both `PaginatedVitals` and `PaginatedBiometrics` bypass Carbon's own row sorting and re-sort the full dataset themselves, so that sorting applies across pages rather than just the visible page. There were two bugs in that arrangement.

### 1. The sort direction was inverted

```js
return sortParams.sortDirection === 'DESC' ? sortingNum : -sortingNum;
```

Every `sortFunc` in `vitals-overview.component.tsx` and `biometrics-base.component.tsx` is an ascending comparator (`a - b`, i.e. negative when `a` sorts first). Carbon treats `ASC` the same way — its `defaultSortRow` returns `compare(cellA, cellB)` for `ASC` and `compare(cellB, cellA)` for `DESC` — and renders the header's `ArrowUp` icon rotated 180° only when the state is `DESC`. So `↑` = `ASC` = smallest/oldest first. The comparator therefore maps directly onto `ASC` and needs negating for `DESC`, which is the reverse of what the code did.

This aligns the rendered order with both the arrow and the header's `aria-sort` value, for every sortable column in these two tables rather than just `Date and time`.

### 2. The sort state was read from the wrong place

Both components recorded the sort state from inside `sortRow`, returning `0` so that Carbon would not reorder anything itself. `sortRow` is the wrong hook for that, for three reasons:

- **Carbon does not treat it as a pure comparator.** `getDerivedStateFromProps` calls `getSortedState` — and therefore `sortRow` — whenever `sortHeaderKey` is already set. Setting state from inside it closed a cycle: a new `sortParams` object → a new `sortedData` array → a new `rows` reference → Carbon's `useEffect([headers, rows])` → `getDerivedStateFromProps` → back into `sortRow`. Before the first click `sortHeaderKey` is `null`, so the cycle never started and the table looked fine, which is why this went unnoticed. Measured with a counter on `usePagination`, a single sort click produced 300+ renders, climbing until the heap was exhausted.
- **Carbon skips it when a header transitions to `NONE`.** The `sortDirection === 'NONE'` branch never fired, so the third click on a header left the rows sorted while `aria-sort` had already reset to `none`.
- **Carbon never invokes it when the page holds a single row**, because `Array.prototype.sort` performs no comparisons on a one-element array. On such a page, clicking a header moved `aria-sort` but left the rows untouched.

The sort state is now captured from the header's `onClick` callback, which Carbon calls exactly once per click with the state it is transitioning to:

```tsx
const handleSortHeaderClick = (
  _event: unknown,
  { sortHeaderKey, sortDirection }: { sortHeaderKey: string; sortDirection: DataTableSortState },
) => {
  setSortParams({ key: sortDirection === 'NONE' ? '' : sortHeaderKey, sortDirection });
};
```

`sortRow` is left as a pure `() => 0`. That covers all three sort states, fixes both of the gaps above, and removes the render loop at its source rather than damping it with a previous-state bailout.

Both tables carried their own copy of all of this — the sort state, the click handler and the block that re-sorts the full dataset were identical line for line, so any future change would ha

## Summary

Refactors the age-based vitals e2e suite (`e2e/specs/age-based-vitals.spec.ts`) to a single table-driven set of scenarios and adds the preschooler (3–<4 years) age group for [O3-4825](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-4825).

Previously each age group only asserted the temperature cell. Now every group (newborn, infant, child, preschooler, adult) runs two scenarios:

- All values sit comfortably inside the normal band, so nothing is flagged. This guards against false positives.
- All values sit comfortably past the critically-high cutoff, so temperature, blood pressure, pulse, and respiratory rate are each flagged critically high.

Pulse, respiratory rate, and blood pressure use age-specific reference ranges, so each group runs against its own generated patient to confirm the correct ranges resolve. Temperature is not age-specific (its range is fixed, splitting only at 3 months), so the same temperature values are used for every group.

Also extracts the `expectCellInterpretation` helper into `e2e/commands/test-helpers.ts` (typed via `VitalInterpretation`) so the assertion is shared instead of hand-rolled per test.

title: (feat) Order basket should try to rely on server-side dates
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary
<!-- Please describe what problems your PR addresses. -->

This PR attempts to address an issue where it still possible for the order basket to attempt to create an order encounter dated to a time which is in the future from the server's perspective. Future-dated encounters are rejected by the backend.

When an order is enqueued, we effectively use the client's date / time as the `startDate` field for the order. Then, when submitting the order we calculate the Encounter date time as the earliest of: the `scheduledDate` of any order, the `startDate` of any order, or the current date. All of these datetimes are client-local. In most circumstances, network delays and processing times means that as long as the client and server are synced to the same NTP server, this is largely unproblematic (NTP drift is normally well < 100ms), but if they are not synced, it possible for the client to be in the future by a small lead from server (a few seconds), which isn't made up form during request submission and processing, resulting in the server rejecting the request.

This tries to work around this problem by inferring, at the time of entry, whether an order is being back-dated or forward-dated ("user-selected date") or just relying on the default (i.e., the order date is the today). If the order date is today, we submit an order (and encounter) with no datetime, allowing the server side to fill in these datetime fields. Because they use the server timestamps, these timestamps should always be earlier or equal to the moment the encounter validation fires.

## Summary

The patient banner moves its "Show more" (toggle contact details) button below the header when the banner is 520px or narrower — for example, when a workspace squeezes the chart. But that check read the DOM ref during render, and the banner's ResizeObserver only stored a coarse "narrower than 1023px" boolean. So a resize that didn't flip the boolean (say, 900px down to 500px) never re-rendered the banner, and the button stayed in the wrong position until something unrelated triggered a render.

The fix stores the observed banner width in state and derives both layout decisions from it, so every resize re-evaluates the layout. Initial-render behavior is unchanged.

Includes tests that drive a mocked ResizeObserver across the 520px threshold and assert the button's position (a `data-testid` was added to the header button column for this). The resize-only scenario was also verified in a real browser: narrowing 900px → 500px without any interaction now moves the button immediately, and widening moves it back.

title: (fix) O3-5824: Keep dashboard grid widgets contained at narrow viewports
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary Dashboard widgets that are wider than the space available to them — like the vitals table — spill past the edge of the page and get cut off. There's no scrollbar, so the cut-off content (the SpO2 column, the table pagination, the Add button) is effectively hidden. This happens on tablets, on smaller desktop windows, and at any desktop size when an open workspace narrows the chart. Two CSS Grid defaults cause it: 1. The single-column dashboard layout uses a plain `1fr` column, which can't shrink below its content's natural width. The two-column layout already avoids this with `minmax(0, 1fr)`. 2. The widgets are grid items, which default to `min-width: auto` and also refuse to shrink below their content. This PR fixes both: the single-column layout now uses `minmax(0, 1fr)`, and widgets get `min-width: 0`. Fixing only the column is not enough — the widget itself still overflows (verified: the column shrank to 678px while the widget stayed at 831px). With both in place, widgets stay contained and Carbon's built-in table scrolling takes over, so wide tables scroll inside their own cards. Tested at every width from 672px to 1920px, on both sides of each layout breakpoint, and with a workspace open: nothing is clipped, and the two-column layout on large screens is unchanged. Full measurements are in the ticket. ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## Related Issue https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5824 ## Other

Both the Diagnoses column in the visit history table and the expanded visit summary aggregate every encounter's diagnoses without deduplication before passing them to `DiagnosisTags`. The list is sorted by rank before deduplication, so a diagnosis that is primary in any encounter of the visit shows as primary. This is a display-level change only. Encounter-level diagnosis records are unchanged, and per-encounter data still reflects every assertion as recorded. ## Screenshots ### Before Duplicate "Diabetes mellitus" tags ### After Only one top-level "Diabetes mellitus" tag ## Related Issue https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5822 ## Other The ticket flags deduplicating non-coded diagnoses by exact text as a proposed display rule rather than settled behavior. The form engine registers its built-in `endpoint` data source (openmrs/openmrs-ngx-formentry#178) once, when `FormEntryModule` is constructed. The fix re-registers a fresh `EndpointDataSource` right after the clearing step, before the configurable data sources, so a custom data source registered under the same name still overrides it.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Adds a "Print visit summary" button to each visit row in the patient chart's Visits tab. Clicking it opens a modal that previews the visit summary PDF inline, with a Download button always available in the footer as a fallback for browsers that cannot render the PDF in an iframe.

The button and modal live in `esm-patient-label-printing-app`, which already depends on the `patientdocuments` backend module (it hosts the existing patient identifier sticker printing). The button registers into the `visit-detail-overview-actions` slot at order 2, after the edit and delete visit buttons.

The PDF is fetched from the existing backend endpoint `GET /ws/rest/v1/patientdocuments/visitSummary?visitUuid=<uuid>` as a blob via `openmrsFetch`, rather than pointing an iframe at the URL directly, so that HTTP failures can be surfaced distinctly. Each failure maps to its own translated message in the modal: 403 (not authorized), 404 (visit not found), any other status (generation failed), and no response (network error).

The button is gated on the `App: Can generate a Visit Summary` privilege and is hidden by default behind the `showPrintVisitSummaryButton` config flag (default `false`), matching the pattern of the existing sticker button.

## Dependencies

This is the frontend half of the feature. For it to be usable by non-admin users on a distribution:

- The `patientdocuments` module version shipped must contain the visit summary endpoint (present on `main`, `1.2.0-SNAPSHOT`; not in the released `1.1.0`). `backendDependencies` is left at the current bound and should be tightened to `>=1.2.0` once that version is released.
- The `App: Can generate a Visit Summary` privilege must be registered on the server. It is currently enforced by the backend but not created at startup, so on a fresh install only superusers pass the check. Tracked separately as a backend fix.

See existing PR titles for inspiration.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The Angular form engine passes a diagnosis question's schema-level datasource config (`datasource.config`, including `conceptSourceUuid`) to `searchOptions` and `resolveSelectedValue`. The `diagnoses` datasource previously ignored it, so no terminology code could be shown next to a diagnosis.

With this change, `findDiagnoses` and `resolveConcept` accept the optional options argument. When it names a `conceptSourceUuid`, the concept search and the selected-value lookup request `conceptMappings` and emit a `code` field on the option, which the form engine renders as `{ICD11CODE} {Name}` per the KNHTS convention. The code comes from the concept's mapping to the configured source, preferring SAME-AS mappings. Concepts without a mapping, and questions without the config, behave exactly as before; other datasources sharing `mapConcept`/`resolveConcept` are unchanged.

## Summary
<!-- Please describe what problems your PR addresses. -->


The OWASP dependency check currently runs on every pull request. In practice, it often fails because of vulnerabilities that already exist in the codebase rather than vulnerabilities introduced by the PR itself. This can mislead contributors into thinking their changes caused the failure.

Also, new vulnerabilities can appear at any time as the OWASP database is updated, even without any code changes.

This PR removes the OWASP check from the pull request workflow and keeps it running only on commits.

If a commit introduces a new vulnerable dependency, the check will still fail on that commit, notifying the merger before the changes are merged. The results will also remain available in the commit history, making it easy to track when a vulnerability was introduced.

title: (fix) Settle previous-encounter Promise so form loads can't hang
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

`PatientPreviousEncounterService.getPreviousEncounter` wraps an RxJS subscription in a `Promise` but left two paths unsettled:

- the error callback only logged via `console.error` and never called `reject()`, so a failed encounters request left the Promise pending forever; and
- the `if (encounters)` block had no `else`, so a `null`/`undefined` response also never settled.

`fe-wrapper.component.ts` `mergeMap`s the form-load pipeline into this Promise, so an unsettled Promise leaves the form workspace stuck in a loading state with no error surfaced, since the swallowed error never reaches the pipeline's `catchError`.

This change rejects on the error path and resolves to an empty result on a falsy response so both paths settle. A new spec covers the match, no-match, null-response, and both failure paths.
