body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

When starting a visit with an extension field filled in (e.g. selecting an appointment to fulfill, or billing details), clicking **Start visit** could show the "Close workspace(s)" unsaved-changes confirmation modal even though the visit was being saved successfully.

This happens because of a race in the submit flow of `exported-visit-form.workspace.tsx`:

1. The visit `POST` succeeds, and the SWR invalidations (`invalidateVisitAndEncounterData` / `invalidateCurrentVisit`) kick off a revalidation of the active visit.
2. The submit handler then awaits the post-save extension callbacks (appointment `status-change` check-in, billing extra-visit info) before calling `closeWorkspace({ discardUnsavedChanges: true })`.
3. While those callbacks are in flight, the revalidated active visit causes `usePatientChartPatientAndVisit` to relaunch the patient chart workspace group with a new visit context. The framework treats this implicit relaunch as closing the open workspaces, finds the visit form still reporting `hasUnsavedChanges={isDirty}`, and prompts the user to discard changes that were already saved.

Whether the modal appears depends purely on whether the extension callback request finishes before or after the active-visit revalidation, which is why it reproduces intermittently on some servers (seen on test3) and not others (dev3) running the same code. Delaying the appointment `status-change` response by 4s reproduces it deterministically on both.

The fix makes the form stop reporting unsaved changes as soon as the visit create/update request resolves successfully (both the online and offline paths). From that moment the user's input is persisted, so whatever wins the race, the workspace-group relaunch finds nothing dirty and no prompt is shown.

Note: with this change, if a post-save extension callback fails (the form currently stays open with an error snackbar), closing the workspace afterwards no longer prompts. That seems correct, since the visit already exists and resubmitting the form would create a second visit.

Other Workspace2 forms that await secondary requests after a successful primary save while keeping `hasUnsavedChanges` bound to form dirtiness may have the same latent race and are worth auditing.

## Screenshots

Before -

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09364ff6-d92c-4e5b-97a8-50b73f61dcda


After - 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c4c9c93-4c2a-4a7f-bb16-09a5e52e4434


## Related Issue
https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5738

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Adds test coverage for form validation paths that previously had none, splitting assertions by level: exact per-message checks live in unit tests, while e2e tests assert the user journey.

- **Unit** (`drug-order-form.test.tsx`): submitting an empty drug order surfaces every required-field error (dosage, route, frequency, indication, quantity to dispense, refills) and does not save. Verified by mutation: temporarily relaxing the route schema makes the test fail on exactly "Route is required".
- **E2E, drug orders**: saving a drug order with missing required fields is blocked, the basket item stays Incomplete, and filling the fields produces a New order.
- **E2E, vitals (empty form)**: the save button is disabled while the form is pristine, and submitting a dirtied-then-cleared form shows the "Please fill at least one field" error.
- **E2E, vitals (out of range)**: saving SpO2 101 shows the field-level range error and the invalid-values notification. The test first verifies via API that the SpO2 concept defines `hiAbsolute` below 101, so a misconfigured environment fails fast with a clear message instead of a mystery failure. It also waits for the input's `max` attribute to be populated before saving, because the client-side range check silently no-ops until the `conceptreferencerange` request resolves (the test raced this under parallel load and the form saved 101 successfully).
- **E2E, visits**: starting a visit without selecting a visit type shows the "Missing visit type" error and no visit starts. This is folded into the existing start-and-end-visit journey rather than a standalone test, since the error strings themselves are already covered by `visit-form.test.tsx`; the e2e adds the recovery path (fix the error, then a real save succeeds).

title: (fix) Deduplicate overlapping test result branches in the results viewer
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary Follow-up to #3345. The results viewer receives the same physical observation through several obstree branches: the default `resultsViewerConcepts` roots overlap (Bloodwork contains Hematology), and each root's tree carries a full copy of a concept's obs list. The filter reducer merged same-flatName duplicates by concatenating those copies, so one result was held N times. The visible symptoms and related edge cases: - The "Results (N)" header overcounts: one Platelets result shows "Results (2)", two results show "Results (4)", while the table renders a single row. - Two genuinely distinct results with the same value and datetime (one result per order, entered against the same encounter) collapse into one row, because de-duplication keyed on `datetime + value` cannot tell a copy from a real duplicate. - Filtering by a checkbox whose branch was collapsed into another branch's row hides that row even though the count still includes it. ### Fix Treat obs lists, not individual obs, as the unit of de-duplication. Branch copies are whole-list copies, so equal obs *within* one list are distinct real results while equal lists *across* branches are duplicates: - `filter-reducer`: same-flatName duplicates now merge with a multiset union (for each `obsDatetime + value` identity, keep the highest count seen in any single branch) instead of concatenating. The merge also copies nodes instead of mutating them, so the SWR-cached trees are no longer modified and `INITIALIZE` is idempotent across re-dispatches. - `filter-context`: a normalized branch list (keyed by rendered panel + `conceptUuid`) collapses duplicate branches that differ in flatName, using the same multiset merge. `tableData`, `timelineData`, `totalResultsCount`, and `filteredResultsCount` all derive from this one list, so the header count is structurally aligned with the rendered rows. Entries carry the flatNames that collapsed into them. - `tree-view` / `grouped-timeline`: checkbox filtering matches entries against all contributing flatNames, so filtering by either alias of a collapsed branch keeps the row visible. This preserves the behavior #3345 established: the same concept legitimately rendered under two different panels stays as two rows. One intentional change in the Over time view: a branch collapsed in the table is now also collapsed in the timeline instead of appearing once per source branch. ## Screenshots ### Before Results count is 4 yet the list only has one row Results count is 5 yet the list only has four rows ### After Results counts match row counts ## Related Issue ## Other The `obsDatetime + value` identity is the best available until the backend exposes obs uuids. A follow-up to add `uuid` to the obs

title: (fix) Allow recording allergies from the order basket outside the patient chart
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The "Add allergy" (+) control that appears in the order basket's drug search launches the allergy form. That form is registered to the `patient-chart` workspace group and reads the patient from its group props, so it only works inside the patient chart. When the order basket runs outside the chart (for example, in the ward app), the `patient-chart` group isn't active, so launching the form opened that group with null group props and crashed every action button registered to it (orders, notes, forms, vitals) with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'patientUuid')`.

This decouples the allergy form from the chart group, following the same pattern the order basket itself already uses to run outside the chart:

- Extract a presentational `AllergyForm`, and add an `exportedAllergyFormWorkspace` that sources the patient from window props. Hosts register it into their own workspace window so it opens in their group rather than the chart's.
- The "add allergy" control now uses an optional, host-provided `launchAllergyForm`. Inside the chart it still launches the chart workspace (behavior unchanged); outside the chart the host launches the exported workspace as a child of its own window. The launcher is threaded through the exported add-drug-order workspace and the `allergy-list-pills-slot`.

The ward registration that consumes this lives in the companion PR openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-management#2561.

## Screenshots

### Behavior (in the ward order basket, which renders the order basket outside the chart):

#### **Before:** clicking the allergy **+** raised a stack of `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'patientUuid')` errors and the form never opened.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33e5371b-6b7e-431c-b65d-7d35a475d81e

#### **After:** the allergy form opens cleanly within the ward, with no console errors, and closing it returns to the order basket.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a610dae8-ebdf-4592-9fd6-89a8d5967dc9

title: (fix) Recalculate revised medication quantities
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a conventional commit label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below.
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

When the outpatient-quantity setting is on, the drug order form auto-calculates "Quantity to dispense" from `dose × frequencyPerDay × duration`. This works for new orders, but silently broke for **revise** and **renew**: editing the dose or duration on an existing order recomputed nothing, and no recalculate link ever appeared.

The cause is how an order's frequency is reconstructed. `buildMedicationOrder` (`api/api.ts`) hardcodes `frequencyPerDay: null` because the value isn't on the order payload. OpenMRS core models `frequencyPerDay` on the `OrderFrequency` definition, and the REST layer serializes an order's frequency as a `REF` (uuid + display only), so the per-day multiplier is dropped. With it null, `calculatedQuantity` is always null on a revised order, so the form can't offer a recalculation until the clinician re-picks the frequency from the dropdown.

### What changed

- Resolve `frequencyPerDay` from the order config (`orderFrequencies`) by frequency UUID when the watched frequency doesn't carry it. That config is the same definition the backend treats as the source of truth. Freshly selected frequencies keep using their own value.
- Only show the "Apply calculated quantity" link when the calculated value differs from the current quantity, so an inherited (or deliberately set) quantity stays put on open and the link surfaces only when there's a real discrepancy to act on.

Manual overrides stay sticky and quantities are never auto-overwritten; recalculation remains an explicit, opt-in click.

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

This PR fixes a bug where lab results were displayed multiple times in the patient-chart lab results viewer. The root cause was that the de-duplication key used `flatName` instead of `conceptUuid`, causing the same observation to render once per order branch. The fix keys de-duplication on `conceptUuid` so identical observations (same concept + datetime + value) collapse into a single row.

### Problem

On the patient-chart lab results viewer, a single lab result is rendered multiple times — once per order placed for that test. A NEW order plus its auto-generated DISCONTINUE order made the same result show twice; two orders, four times, and so on.

### Root cause

The /obstree backend returns the same orderable-test concept under several branches of the orderable-tests tree (effectively one branch per order), each branch carrying the same single observation. In filter-context's tableData builder the de-duplication key is based on test.flatName, which differs per branch, so the identical observation is not collapsed and renders once per branch.

### Fix

Key the de-duplication on the observation's conceptUuid instead of flatName. The same observation (same concept + datetime + value) reached via different branches now collapses to a single row, while genuinely different tests stay separate. One-line change, no new dependencies, no new i18n keys.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Builds on #3332. After that fix landed, a secondary issue remained: if the visit context changed *while* a workspace group launch was already in progress, the in-flight launch would complete with stale props and no relaunch would follow.

This PR replaces the inline async logic in `usePatientChartPatientAndVisit` with a `launchLatestWorkspaceGroup` callback that uses a while loop to re-read `latestWorkspaceGroupProps` after each resolved launch. If props changed while a launch was pending, the loop picks up the latest visit context and relaunches immediately — no separate effect run needed.

Also removes the redundant `launchWorkspaceGroup2` call from `VisitForm`. That call was a holdover from before the hook handled relaunching reactively; keeping it caused a double-launch on visit save.

## Screenshots

## Related Issue

https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5707

## Other

Adds a regression test that directly exercises the mid-flight race: holds the first launch via a controlled promise, changes the active visit while it's pending, resolves the first launch, and asserts the while loop picks up the latest visit and relaunches.

title: (fix) Don't label naturally expired medications as Discontinued
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The medications summary in the visit detail overview was tagging any order with `autoExpireDate <= now` as **Discontinued**, conflating two distinct order lifecycle states: clinician-initiated discontinuation (`dateStopped` set) and natural completion of a duration-bound course (`autoExpireDate` reached).

OpenMRS core treats these as separate predicates — [`Order#isDiscontinued`](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-core/blob/main/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/Order.java#L593) checks `dateStopped`, [`Order#isExpired`](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-core/blob/main/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/Order.java#L633) checks `autoExpireDate` — and the FHIR2 translator maps them to `CANCELLED` and `STOPPED` respectively. The medications details table elsewhere in this codebase already gates the **Discontinued** tag on `dateStopped` alone (`packages/esm-patient-medications-app/src/components/medications-details-table.component.tsx`); the visits panel was the outlier.

### What changed

- `isPastMedication` → `isDiscontinued` so the helper name matches the tag it gates.
- The `autoExpireDate` branch is removed; reaching `autoExpireDate` is natural completion, not discontinuation.
- Comparison switches to strict `<`, matching core's `checkDate.after(dateStopped)` semantics, so a future-scheduled `dateStopped` no longer pre-emptively shows the tag.
- The previous `action === 'DISCONTINUE'` branch is dropped: a discontinuation order is a separate row pointing at the original via `previousOrder`; the original is the one whose `dateStopped` gets set, so tagging the discontinuation row "Discontinued" was labeling the wrong order.

## Screenshots


## Related Issue

No Jira ticket — discovered while reviewing #3043, which bundles this same fix inside the (unrelated) O3-5378 scheduled-date feature work. Landing this PR first separates the concerns so #3043 can rebase to focus on the feature.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

This PR fixes an issue where the `patient-chart workspace` group kept stale `groupProps` after the visit context changed.

Previously, the workspace group was launched only once on mount using a boolean ref. If the visit context later changed — for example when a visit ended or a new one started — the patient chart store was updated but `launchWorkspaceGroup2` was never called again, causing workspaces opened from the patient chart to receive stale visit props.

This change tracks the UUID of the last successfully launched visit context and relaunches the workspace group whenever that UUID changes. The launch state is only recorded after `launchWorkspaceGroup2` returns true, so a user declining to close unsaved workspaces does not suppress future re-launch attempts.

A microfrontend for [OpenMRS 3](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org) that records, displays, and manages clinical procedures in the patient chart.

- **Procedures detailed summary** — full-page table that adds procedure type, body site, start/end timestamps, status, and inline notes. Rows are expandable to show additional detail without leaving the page.
- **Record & edit form** — a side-panel workspace for creating and updating procedures. Supports:
  - Fuzzy concept search for procedure name, body site, status, and duration unit — all driven by configurable concept UUIDs.
  - Exact start date/time or estimated start date (year + optional month) for procedures where the precise date is not known.
  - End date/time and duration with unit.
  - Procedure type selection from the OpenMRS procedure type registry.
  - Free-text notes.
- **Delete confirmation** — modal that voids a procedure record.

---

#### Backend

This app requires the [openmrs-module-emrapi](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-emrapi) module, which exposes the `/ws/rest/v1/procedure` REST endpoints used for all CRUD operations.


---

## Configuration

The app is configured through the [OpenMRS config system](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/loading-modules#module-configuration). All keys live under `@openmrs/esm-patient-procedures-app`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |

| `detailedViewPageSize` | Number | `10` | Rows per page in the procedures detailed summary view. |
| `procedureConceptUuid` | UUID | `8d490bf4-…` | Scopes the procedure concept search. |
| `procedureConceptSourceType` | String | `Concept class` | How `procedureConceptUuid` filters results: `Concept class`, `Concept set`, `Answer to`, or `any`. |
| `bodySiteConceptUuid` | UUID | `8d491c7a-…` (Anatomy) | Scopes the body-site concept search. |
| `bodySiteConceptSourceType` | String | `Concept class` | Same options as above. |
| `statusConceptUuid` | UUID | `167157AAAA…` | Scopes the status concept search. |
| `statusConceptSourceType` | String | `Concept set` | Same options as above. |
| `durationUnitConceptUuid` | UUID | `1732AAAAA…` | Scopes the duration-unit concept search. |
| `durationUnitConceptSourceType` | String | `Answer to` | Same options as above. |

---

## Form fields

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Procedure | Yes | Fuzzy concept search |
| Procedure type | Yes | Dropdown from `/ws/rest/v1/proceduretype` |
| Body site | Yes | Fuzzy concept search |

title: (fix) O3-5691: Persist medication renewals with action=RENEW
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary When the clinician clicks **Renew** on a medication tile, `prepMedicationOrderPostData` was rewriting the basket item's `action: 'RENEW'` to `action: 'NEW'` before POSTing to `/encounter`. The resulting `DrugOrder` was persisted with `order_action='NEW'` and `previous_order_id` set, instead of `order_action='RENEW'`. This change flips the one constant at `api.ts:179` so the user-selected action is preserved end-to-end: - Renewals in the database carry `order_action='RENEW'`, making renewals distinguishable from prospective new orders without joining on `previous_order_id`. - The FHIR API's existing `RENEW → basedOn` branch in `MedicationRequestTranslatorImpl` now fires for O3-placed renewals, so external consumers can walk the chain. Once [FM2-680](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/FM2-680) lands, the canonical `priorPrescription` field will also populate. - The wiki's "internal translation in O3" gotcha [Order Entry in O3: A PM Reference](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/docs/pages/1031766039/Order+Entry+in+O3+A+PM+Reference) goes away for new renewals. ### Backend behaviour Verified against my local distro running O3 v3.6.0: - `OrderServiceImpl.saveOrder` treats `action=NEW` (with `previousOrder` set) and `action=RENEW` identically for the save path — same auto-stop logic (neither stops the previous order), same orderable-match check, same active-orders ambiguity check. The rewrite was never satisfying a backend constraint. - End-to-end renewal placed via the patched UI lands as `ORD-393 RENEW previous=392`, original keeps running. FHIR returns `basedOn: [{ reference, identifier: "ORD-392" }]`. ## Screenshots ## Related Issue https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5691 Also related: - [FM2-680](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/FM2-680) — FHIR translator populates `priorPrescription` for any order with `previousOrder`. Complementary fix on the backend side. - [O3-5169](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5169) / #2949 — the PR that originally introduced the rewrite. ## Other ### Note for implementations Reports or dashboards filtering on `order_action='NEW'` will start excluding renewals after this change. Implementations that rely on the previous behaviour can adjust to `order_action IN ('NEW','RENEW')`. Historical renewals placed before this fix remain stored as `order_action='NEW'` with `previous_order_id` set. ### Follow-up not addressed here 1. `packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-basket/general-order-type/resources.ts:32-46` has a similar pattern for non-drug orders. Its NEW-or-RENEW branch doesn't include `previousOrder` at all — a deeper, separate bug worth its own ticket. 2. [FM2-680](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/FM2-680) [FM2-680]: https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/FM2-680?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

body:

## Summary

Adopts the happy-dom-by-default pattern that `openmrs-esm-core` already uses across its 25 per-package vitest configs, with per-file `/** @vitest-environment jsdom */` docblocks as the escape hatch for tests that hit happy-dom/jsdom divergences. See [`esm-navigation/src/history/history.test.ts`](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core/blob/e1470604dafd40c0e687b75b8838278061c511db/packages/framework/esm-navigation/src/history/history.test.ts#L2) in core for the established precedent — only 1 of 104 test files in core needs the override.

### Changes
- `tools/vitest.shared.ts`: `environment: 'jsdom'` → `'happy-dom'`.
- `package.json`: add `happy-dom@^20.0.0`. Keep `jsdom@^28.0.0` because six test files in this repo still need it via the docblock escape hatch.
- Add `/** @vitest-environment jsdom */` to six test files where happy-dom diverges:
  - `esm-patient-chart-app/.../end-visit-dialog.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-immunizations-app/.../immunizations-form.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-medications-app/.../add-drug-order.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-notes-app/.../visit-notes-form.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-orders-app/.../lab-results-form.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-programs-app/.../programs-form.test.tsx`

  Most share the same root cause: happy-dom's `Date` and `AbortController` instances do not satisfy `instanceof` against the host realm's constructors, which breaks `expect.any(Date)` and `expect.objectContaining(...)` matchers on payloads that production code constructs with `new Date()` / `new AbortController()`. The `lab-results-form.test.tsx` file fails differently (a form-submit callback never fires under happy-dom) and gets the same escape hatch.

### Why bother

Benchmarked on `esm-patient-chart-app` (27 test files / 144 tests):

| | wall-clock median | tests passing |
|---|---|---|
| jest (pre-migration) | 6.39s | 117/117 |
| vitest + jsdom (status quo) | 9.03s | 143/143 (+ 1 skipped) |
| **vitest + happy-dom (this PR)** | **6.42s** | **143/143** (+ 1 skipped) |

A 29% wall-clock drop versus jsdom, and effectively parity with the pre-migration jest baseline. Savings scale with the number of test files because environment init is a per-file cost.

happy-dom's transitive dep tree is also smaller.

## Screenshots

N/A — tooling change only.

## Related Issue

N/A

## Other

`yarn turbo run typescript` (20 workspaces) and `yarn turbo run lint` (21 workspaces) are both green locally. All 135 test files pass across the 20 testable workspaces.

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Submitting a medication order fails with `Encounter.datetimeShouldBeInVisitDatesRange` when the user-selected start date falls before the visit's start datetime:

```json
{
  "code": "webservices.rest.error.invalid.submission",
  "fieldErrors": {
    "encounterDatetime": [{
      "code": "Encounter.datetimeShouldBeInVisitDatesRange",
      "message": "The encounter datetime should be between the visit start and stop dates."
    }]
  }
}
```

#3198 introduced backdating of `encounterDatetime` to the earliest basket `startDate` so the backend's `dateActivated >= encounterDatetime` constraint holds. That fix overlooks a second backend constraint: `Encounter.datetimeShouldBeInVisitDatesRange`. The PR description called this out as a deferred follow-up ("Datetime precision on date-picker floors") with the suggested fix being a "clamp-on-submit (or a schema check against `getStartDateMinimum`)." This PR implements that follow-up.

Backend constraints satisfied (verified against `EncounterValidator.java` and `OrderValidator.java` in `openmrs-core`):

1. `encounterDatetime` must be within `[visit.startDatetime, visit.stopDatetime]` (strict `before`/`after`, so equal-to-boundary is OK).
2. Each order's `dateActivated >= encounterDatetime` (strict `after`).
3. For `REVISE`, the new `dateActivated` must be strictly after the previous order's `dateActivated` because the backend computes `previous.dateStopped = new.dateActivated - 1s`.

Changes:

- **`postOrdersOnNewEncounter`** (`postOrders.ts`) clamps the encounter date to the visit window — floor to `visit.startDatetime`, ceiling at `visit.stopDatetime` — owning the encounter-bounds rule in one place.
- **`getOrdersPayloadFromOrderBasket`** (`postOrders.ts`) floors each basket item's `startDate` to the encounter date before invoking the prep function, so each order's `dateActivated` stays `>= encounterDatetime` after the encounter is clamped. New `floorOrderStartDate` helper.
- **Drug order form** (`drug-order-form.component.tsx`) snaps `data.startDate` up to `startDateMin` in `handleFormSubmission` when it falls below. The picker is date-only and resolves selections to local 00:00, while `startDateMin` is at datetime precision (visit start for NEW/RENEW, `previous.dateActivated + 1s` for REVISE). The snap covers the time-of-day component the picker cannot represent.

Follow-up to #3198 (originally tracked as [O3-4444](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-4444)).

`orderEncounterType` config-schema duplication between `esm-patient-medications-app` and `esm-patient-orders-app` and the visit-disabled-install backdating path remain as the deferred items from #3198.

This switches things so that a warning is shown to the user, but the warning is non-blocking. The "dose number" for vaccinations is a sequence number in a schedule and not an incrementing counter of the number of times a patient has been given a dose. As Andy Kanter has repeatedly pointed out as we've developed immunization-related functionality, ["just because a person gets a shot doesn't mean the shot was valid"](https://talk.openmrs.org/t/immunization-vs-vaccination/30144/9). Consequently, blocking users from submitting a record of a second application of the same dose forces users to record clinically incorrect data. Presumably, we should have some way of marking known-bad or known-erroneous doses as such, but that's beyond the scope of this ticket. ## Screenshots ## Related Issue https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/O3-4578 ## Other

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Mirrors openmrs/openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib#669 in patient-chart. Migrates the two remaining `/conceptreferences` callers from a chunked GET pattern (`chunk(uuids, 10)` plus `Promise.all` over N requests) to a single POST that takes the references array in the body.

Affected hooks:

- `esm-generic-patient-widgets-app`: `useConcepts`
- `esm-patient-tests-app`: `useOrderReasons`

Benefits:

- One round trip per render instead of `ceil(N / 10)`. A widget configured with 50 concepts goes from 5 sequential SWR fetches to 1.
- Removes the implicit cap from chunking against an unstated URL-length limit. POST sidesteps URL-length concerns entirely.
- Cleaner failure semantics: one request, one error path, no risk of silently merging partial results from multiple chunks.

Behavior preserved end-to-end: both hooks return the same `{ concepts, isLoading }` / `{ orderReasons, isLoading }` shape, the empty-input short-circuit (`null` SWR key) still applies, and consumers (`useObs`, `test-order-form`) are untouched.

## Screenshots

## Related Issue

## Other

Requires REST API >= 4.0.0, when `POST /conceptreferences` landed. No formal floor declaration mechanism exists in patient-chart (none was added for the form-engine-lib precedent either), so this is documented here rather than enforced.

body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary i18next escapes interpolated values by default to guard against XSS, so a drug name like `Nystatin creme vaginale 100000UI/g` was rendering as `Nystatin creme vaginale 100000UI/g` in the "Order pinned" snackbar subtitle, because the subtitle is plain text and the entity is never decoded. The same applies to apostrophes (`'`) in names like `Motrin Children's 100mg/5ml`. This passes `interpolation: { escapeValue: false }` to the two affected `t()` calls (pin and unpin). The snackbar renders the result as text, not HTML, so disabling escape is safe and the drug name displays verbatim. Verified locally against a backend with 35 affected drugs (forward slashes and/or apostrophes in names) — all render correctly after the fix. ## Screenshots ### Before: ### After: drug name renders verbatim (e.g. `Nystatin creme vaginale 100000UI/g`, `Motrin Children's 100mg/5ml`). ## Related Issue ## Other @VeronicaMuthee we should fix the typo in the `Motrin Children's 100mg/5ml` formulation (it currently reads 'Chilren' instead of 'Children')

Two clinicians on different sessions could still race to create duplicates. Bumps [dompurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify) from 3.3.2 to 3.4.1.
Release notes

Sourced from dompurify's releases.

DOMPurify 3.4.1

  • Fixed an issue with on-handler stripping for HTML-spec-reserved custom element names (font-face, color-profile, missing-glyph, font-face-src, font-face-uri, font-face-format, font-face-name) under permissive CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING
  • Fixed a case-sensitivity gap in the annotation-xml check that allowed mixed-case variants to bypass the basic-custom-element exclusion in XHTML mode
  • Fixed SANITIZE_NAMED_PROPS repeatedly prefixing already-prefixed id and name values on subsequent sanitization
  • Fixed the IN_PLACE root-node check to explicitly guard against non-string nodeName (DOM-clobbering robustness)
  • Removed a duplicate slot entry from the default HTML attribute allow-list
  • Strengthened the fast-check fuzz harness with explicit XSS invariants, an expanded seed-payload corpus, an additional idempotence property for SANITIZE_NAMED_PROPS, and a negative-control assertion ensuring the invariants actually fire
  • Added regression and pinning tests covering the above fixes and two accepted-behavior contracts (SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES greedy scrub, hook-added attribute handling)
  • Extended CodeQL analysis to run on 3.x and 2.x maintenance branches

DOMPurify 3.4.0

Most relevant changes:

  • Fixed a problem with FORBID_TAGS not winning over ADD_TAGS, thanks @​kodareef5
  • Fixed several minor problems and typos regarding MathML attributes, thanks @​DavidOliver
  • Fixed ADD_ATTR/ADD_TAGS function leaking into subsequent array-based calls, thanks @​1Jesper1
  • Fixed a missing SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES scrub in RETURN_DOM path, thanks @​bencalif
  • Fixed a prototype pollution via CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING, thanks @​trace37labs
  • Fixed an issue with ADD_TAGS function form bypassing FORBID_TAGS, thanks @​eddieran
  • Fixed an issue with ADD_ATTR predicates skipping URI validation, thanks @​christos-eth
  • Fixed an issue with USE_PROFILES prototype pollution, thanks @​christos-eth
  • Fixed an issue leading to possible mXSS via Re-Contextualization, thanks @​researchatfluidattacks and others
  • Fixed an issue with closing tags leading to possible mXSS, thanks @​frevadiscor
  • Fixed a problem with the type dentition patcher after Node version bump
  • Fixed freezing BS runs by reducing the tested browsers array
  • Bumped several dependencies where possible
  • Added needed files for OpenSSF scorecard checks

title: (fix) O3-5618: Validate condition selection before submit triggers
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The conditions form allowed users to click **Save & close** after typing arbitrary text in the condition search box, without actually selecting a concept from the results. This would trigger form submission, briefly show a loading spinner, and then silently bail, leaving the form stuck.

### Root Cause

The `conditionName` field served a dual purpose: it stored the raw search text *and* was the field Zod validated for "did the user select a condition?". Since Zod only checked whether the string was non-empty, any typed text, even garbage passed validation. The actual concept selection was tracked in a separate local `selectedCondition` state that Zod had no visibility into.

### Fix

Separated the two concerns into two distinct fields:

- **`conditionName`**: continues to hold the raw search input text (drives the search box display). No validation rule.
- **`conditionUuid`**: a new hidden field that holds the UUID of the selected concept. This is what Zod validates. It is only set when the user explicitly clicks a result from the dropdown.

### Changes

**`conditions-form.workspace.tsx`**
- Replaced `conditionName` with  `conditionUuid` in the Zod schema
- Relaxed `conditionName` to a plain `z.string()` with no validation rule
- Added `conditionUuid: ''` to `defaultValues`
- Changed `mode` from `'all'` to `'onSubmit'`: validation now runs on submit, not on every keystroke, which is consistent with the form's intent

**`conditions-widget.component.tsx`**
- Added `setValue` to the `useFormContext` destructure
- `handleConditionChange`: on concept click, calls `setValue('conditionUuid', selectedCondition.uuid, { shouldValidate: true })` to write the UUID and immediately clear the error if one was showing
- Search `onChange`: calls `setValue('conditionUuid', '')` on every keystroke to deselect any prior concept pick
- Search `onClear`: similarly clears `conditionUuid`
- All error UI references (`className`, `aria-labelledby`, `renderIcon`, error message paragraph) updated from `errors?.conditionName` → `errors?.conditionUuid`
- Added `setIsSubmittingForm(false)` in the `handleCreate` early-return guard as a safety net for any edge case where the function is reached without a valid selection


## Screenshots

Earlier:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33413c0d-7c6f-497c-9b42-c2b447e64596



Now:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd5b354d-2a84-4578-8e7e-1fdf58a3cc55

https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5618

title: (feat) Surface BMI reference ranges in the biometrics table
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary Persists BMI as its own observation on the vitals and biometrics encounter so the backend can apply the concept reference ranges (including the criteria-based ranges landing in [openmrs/openmrs-content-referenceapplication-demo#63](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-content-referenceapplication-demo/pull/63)) and sets the FHIR `Observation.interpretation`. Styles the biometrics table cells the same way the vitals table is styled today, so weight, height, MUAC and BMI all light up when out of range. - Adds a `bodyMassIndexUuid` config key defaulting to CIEL 1342. - Includes the BMI concept in the biometrics FHIR query and maps it to the `bmi` row key in `useVitalsAndBiometrics`. Keeps the client-side `calculateBodyMassIndex` fallback, gated on there being no stored BMI obs, so historical encounters still display a BMI value. - On form submit, pushes a fresh BMI obs whenever weight or height was touched; voids any prior BMI obs on edit. The calculation effect clears `computedBodyMassIndex` when either input is missing so a stale BMI is never persisted. - Renders biometrics cells via `NumericObservation` with the column's `conceptUuid` and the patient uuid, mirroring the vitals table. `NumericObservation` uses the backend-set interpretation when present and falls back to a patient-aware concept reference range lookup when it isn't — which means historical rows still get styled correctly. ## Screenshots BMI cell styled as `low` (peach background, down arrow) for a 28-year-old male with BMI 18 against the backend's BMI reference range (`lowNormal: 18.5`): BMI not computed or saved if one of the dependent values is not provided: End-to-end network trace showing BMI persisted as an obs on save: ``` POST /ws/rest/v1/encounter → 201 Created obs: - Weight (kg): 55.0 - Height (cm): 175.0 - Body mass index: 18.0 ← persisted via bodyMassIndexUuid ``` ## Related Issue Part of the reference ranges work under [O3-4585](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-4585). Depends on the `1.8.0-SNAPSHOT` bump in openmrs/openmrs-distro-referenceapplication#1004 and, for the criteria-based ranges to actually be evaluated by the backend, on the demo content update Ian Bacher flagged in openmrs/openmrs-content-referenceapplication-demo#63. ## Other - Unit tests updated in `biometrics-overview.test.tsx` and `vitals-biometrics-form.test.tsx` covering: BMI persistence on create, void-and-replace on edit when weight/height change, and `NumericObservation` receiving the right `conceptUuid` / `interpretation` / `patientUuid` for each column. - Weight, height, and MUAC cells are now also styled via `NumericObservation`. Today this means they pick up interpretations the backend already sets; no behaviour change for concepts without reference ranges loaded. title: (fix) O3-5444: Show inline warning when adding a duplicate condition
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done, including the ticket number if there is a ticket. - [x] My work conforms to the [OpenMRS 3.0 Styleguide](https://om.rs/styleguide) and [Contributing Guidelines](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines). - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary Addresses [O3-5444](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5444): The Conditions module currently allows the same condition to be added to a patient's problem list multiple times with no warning. This creates duplicate clinical records. This PR adds an **inline warning** (using Carbon's `InlineNotification`) that appears when a clinician selects a condition that already exists on the patient's problem list. The warning: - **Matches on condition concept alone** (not filtered by clinical status), per the design discussion on the JIRA ticket - **Shows different messages** depending on the existing condition's status: - **Active match**: _"Diabetes mellitus is already on this patient's active problem list. Saving will create a duplicate record."_ - **Inactive match**: _"Diabetes mellitus was previously recorded but is now inactive. You may want to edit the existing record to reactivate it instead."_ - **Is non-blocking** — the clinician can still save if they have a valid clinical reason (e.g., recurrent conditions with different onset dates) - **Disappears** when the search input is cleared This approach follows the inline warning pattern already used in the allergies module (`allergy-form.workspace.tsx`) and aligns with the design feedback from @ibacher and @burkemamlin on the JIRA ticket. ### Why this approach A previous attempt ([PR #3055](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart/pull/3055)) was declined because it used a blocking confirmation modal and lacked test coverage. This PR addresses both concerns: - Uses an **inline warning** instead of a modal, as recommended by @ibacher - Matches on **concept alone** (not concept + status), as recommended by @burkemamlin - Includes **5 new test cases** covering all scenarios ## Screenshots ### Before (no warning — duplicate saved silently) ### After (with fix — warning shown) ## Related Issue https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5444 ## Other N/A [O3-5444]: https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5444?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

title: (fix) O3-4444: Persist medication order start date
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.


## Summary

Persists the user-selected Start date for NEW, RENEW, and REVISE medication orders by sending it as `dateActivated` and aligning the encounter handling with backend semantics.

- **NEW**: the chosen `startDate` is sent as `dateActivated`. The encounter created in the same POST is backdated to the earliest selected date so the backend's `dateActivated >= encounterDatetime` constraint holds.
- **RENEW**: per backend semantics a renewal is a new prescription event, so it now lands in a fresh encounter on the visit with `encounterDatetime` tracking the chosen start date. The form does not inherit `dateActivated` from the previous order.
- **REVISE**: posts against the previous order's existing encounter with the user-selected `dateActivated`. The date picker enforces a minimum of `previous.dateActivated + 1s` so the backend's `previous.dateStopped = new.dateActivated - 1s` computation produces a valid order chain.
- **DISCONTINUE**: unchanged.

Pure helpers extracted for testability: `getEarliestStartDate` (basket → encounter-date derivation) and `getStartDateMinimum` (date picker floor).

### Out of scope (deferred to follow-ups)

- Future-dated orders, handled by `scheduledDate` + `urgency: ON_SCHEDULED_DATE` in #2973.
- Datetime precision on date-picker floors. The picker enforces minimums at calendar-day precision while the backend enforces them at datetime precision. Two instances: a NEW order on the visit's start day yields a `Date` at 00:00 local that can fall before `visit.startDatetime` (triggering `Encounter.datetimeShouldBeInVisitDatesRange`); a same-day REVISE can submit 00:00 for the day, which falls before `previous.dateActivated + 1s`. Cleanest fix is a clamp-on-submit (or a schema check against `getStartDateMinimum`).
- Backdating with a reused encounter on visit-disabled installs. When `orderEncounterUuid` is preset (only on installs that don't support visits and where the user already has an order encounter today), `order-basket.component.tsx` posts orders against that existing encounter without backdating it. A backdated NEW/RENEW will fail the backend's `dateActivated >= encounterDatetime` check. Fix shape: fetch the existing encounter's `encounterDatetime`, and either backdate (if permissible) or create a fresh encounter when the earliest basket `startDate` precedes it.
- `orderEncounterType` is currently duplicated between `esm-patient-medications-app` and `esm-patient-orders-app` config schemas; consolidating into `esm-patient-common-lib` is a follow-up.

## Screenshots

### NEW order with backdated start date

Placed Paracetamol with `Start date` sent to yesterday -> order lands with Start date 05-May-2026 + an encounter dated 05/04/2025 (POST body shows `dateActivated: 2026-05-04T21:00:00Z`).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f340e76f-2123-424c-8c59-44afd5fc12db

### RENEW with backdated start date

Renewed Zyrtec with `Start date` set to yesterday -> renewal lands in a fresh encounter (not the original order's encounter), with `dateActivated: 2026-05-04T21:00:00Z`. The original keeps running until it is discontinued or auto-expires.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e3e3f67-e256-4a90-bd54-4a1535a2755b

### RENEW with default (today)

Renewed Paracetamol without changing `Start date` -> renewal lands today in a separate fresh encounter (proves the new-encounter behaviour irrespective of backdating). 

https://github.com/user-attachm

## Summary

title: (fix) O3-5432: Validate completion date against enrollment date in program enrollment form
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary The program enrollment form let you pick a completion date before the enrollment date and submitted it anyway, which the API rejected with a generic 400 error and no actionable guidance. It also blocked valid same-day completion: the completion picker started at enrollment + 1 day and was disabled outright when the enrollment date was today, even though the backend `PatientProgramValidator` only rejects completion dates strictly before the enrollment date. The form now validates the date order up front with a Zod `superRefine` check that shows an inline error on the completion date field ("Completion date cannot be before the enrollment date"), and the picker constraints are relaxed so the completion date can equal the enrollment date. Same-day completion needs one more nuance: the date picker emits midnight timestamps, which the backend would reject as being before a same-day enrollment. The submitted completion timestamp is therefore aligned to the enrollment timestamp when it falls earlier on the same day, while stored completion times that already fall later that day are preserved on resave. Tests cover the inline validation error, same-day completion in create mode, and preservation of stored same-day completion timestamps in edit mode. ## Screenshots ## Related Issue [O3-5432](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5432) ## Other [O3-5432]: https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5432?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

Keeps duplicate active/upcoming medication search results visible with an "Already prescribed" cue, while disabling duplicate actions to avoid backend overlap errors. 8. - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

- Adds a sticky note to the patient banner — one persistent note per patient, editable in place and voided on delete (matches the O2 coreapps behaviour per @ibacher's feedback).
- CRUD is backed by the REST `obs` resource (`/ws/rest/v1/obs`), keyed on a configurable concept UUID. Using REST rather than FHIR gives us `auditInfo.creator.display` for the provider name shown in the designs.
- Fetched obs are filtered to those with no `encounter` and no `formNamespaceAndPath`, so if a distro's `stickyNoteConceptUuid` overlaps with a concept the visit-note form also writes against, those form-generated obs don't surface here.
- Clicking the header button opens the popover in any non-empty state (skeleton while loading, inline error + retry on failure, or the note). When no note exists, it opens the create modal directly.
- Panel dismissal uses `@openmrs/esm-framework`'s `useOnClickOutside` plus an ESC handler; clicks inside an open edit/delete modal are ignored so they don't collapse the panel underneath.
- If `stickyNoteConceptUuid` is cleared (empty string), the header button is hidden entirely — distros that don't want the feature see nothing.
- Character limit, modal layout, and provider-name footer follow the Zeplin designs.
- Includes unit tests for the panel, header button, create/edit modal, delete modal, and the `isStandaloneStickyNote` filter.

Drug Categories via Concept Sets** Drugs can be grouped into configurable categories using **Concept Sets**, which are managed via **Legacy Admin**. These Concept Sets define how drugs are grouped and can be adapted to local needs (for example, by program, formulary, or service). Each category corresponds to a Concept Set containing the relevant drug concepts. **2. Browse Tab for Browsing Drugs** The drug selection UI has been enhanced with a new **Browse** tab, available **alongside the existing Search tab (which remains the default).** The Browse tab allows users to browse drugs by selecting a category, making it easier to discover medications **without knowing their exact names**. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c53b74e9-d7e5-4bc6-9457-451feba26fc5 **3. Configuration via Implementer Tools** Implementers can control which categories appear in the Browse tab by configuring Concept Set UUIDs under the `drugCategoryConceptSets` setting in `@openmrs/esm-patient-medications-app` via Implementer Tools. Only the configured Concept Sets are exposed to users. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67fea1f8-930f-45e2-8439-ef2b64737015 ## Screenshots ### UI Workflow **Preconditions:** Concept Sets Predefined Meds 1 and Predefined Meds 2 are configured and available. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09556778-4f6a-4623-8068-faac428b0490 ## Related Issue ## Other Sample config: ```jsonc { "@openmrs/esm-patient-medications-app": { "drugCategoryConceptSets": [ "162305AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA", # Heparins "162170AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA" # Sulfonamides ] } } ```
